title: eval-harness: per-prompt CI hooks and thresholded quality gating for prompt regressions
author: Asha Patel
description: Introduce per-prompt CI hooks and a configurable quality gating mechanism to catch prompt-level regressions earlier in the pipeline; motivation: existing eval gates were coarse-grained and missed prompt-specific regressions that caused regressions in production; changes: add per-prompt CI workflow, implement per-prompt hook library that computes per-prompt metrics and fails builds when thresholds are breached, integrate eval-metrics service to report time-series to metrics backend, add docs and test coverage; included a migration script to continue supporting legacy aggregated gates; checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests (rerun flaky evals), [x] docs, [x] Linear ticket linked; impact: improves signal for prompt regressions and reduces noise in aggregated alerts by surfacing failing prompts directly; no breaking API changes
commits: Add per-prompt CI workflow and hook entrypoints
Implement per_prompt_hook.py with threshold evaluation and reporting
Add tests for per-prompt gating and update docs
review_conversation: Miguel Torres: Nice work; can you clarify how thresholds are derived and where they are documented?
Asha Patel: Thresholds default to historical baselines computed by eval-metrics and are configurable per-prompt in config/prompt_gates.yaml; documented in eval-harness/docs/ci.md
Riley Chen: Tests look good but integration CI was flaky; please add retry and limit the heavy eval set to nightly for now
Asha Patel: Added retry logic and reduced per-PR eval sample; left nightly job running the full set

release_notes: Add per-prompt CI hooks and quality gating to detect prompt-level regressions earlier; configurable thresholds and integration with eval-metrics; includes docs and migration for legacy gates
